seed_stills.S: Redraw this same character, facing the viewer (down-screen), in a single still frame. BATTLE STANCE, low and braced, exactly as a baseball batter stands at the plate or a knight stands mid-swing: feet planted wide apart, KNEES CLEARLY BENT, hips low, weight centred between the feet so the body is a stable axis. The mace is gripped at the VERY BASE of its haft — the hand at the bottom end, a pommel grip — so the weapon reaches as far from the body as it possibly can. The mace arm is extended OUT to full reach, level with the shoulder, the mace head held wide and far out. The shield rides on the other forearm, carried close across the chest. Keep EXACTLY the same pixel-art character as the reference: same armour plates, same helm with the gold crown-band and centre ridge, same dark violet/gold palette, same kite shield with its gold rim, same spiked mace, same chunky overworld proportions (big helm, short thick limbs), same slightly elevated three-quarter-overhead camera, same crisp pixel style. Flat solid pure green #00ff00 background, completely empty and unchanged — no scenery, no ground, no shadow, no particles. Camera locked: no zoom, no pan; the figure stays centred at the same size, fully inside the frame with clear green margin on every side. Head level throughout — the helm never bows. Crisp pixel art, no blur, no motion lines, no after-images.

spin_clip_prompt: From this exact battle stance he SPINS in place — the Eye of Reckoning. He pivots around his own centre at a constant fast rate, about 2.5 full revolutions per second (one complete turn every 0.4 seconds, roughly 15 turns across the clip): smooth, constant, no wind-up at the start and no recovery at the end — he is already spinning in the first frame and still spinning in the last. THROUGH THE WHOLE SPIN HE HOLDS THE STANCE: knees stay bent, hips stay low, feet stay planted wide, the body stays the stable axis — he never straightens up, never rises onto his toes, never drifts off centre. The mace stays gripped at the very base of its haft with the arm extended out at full reach, so the mace head sweeps a WIDE circle far outside the body — the weapon is the radius, the body is the axle. The shield stays tucked across the chest. No motion-blur streaks, no smear rings, no after-images, no glow trails, no dust — draw every frame as a clean sharp pixel-art pose. Keep EXACTLY the same pixel-art character as the reference: same armour plates, same helm with the gold crown-band and centre ridge, same dark violet/gold palette, same kite shield with its gold rim, same spiked mace, same chunky overworld proportions (big helm, short thick limbs), same slightly elevated three-quarter-overhead camera, same crisp pixel style. Flat solid pure green #00ff00 background, completely empty and unchanged — no scenery, no ground, no shadow, no particles. Camera locked: no zoom, no pan; the figure stays centred at the same size, fully inside the frame with clear green margin on every side. Head level throughout — the helm never bows. Loop: the last frame matches the first.
